3.1.1.locator: S3 user guide 'Protecting data in transit with encryption' (TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 supported across all API endpoints); AWS announcement 'TLS 1.2 to become the minimum TLS protocol level for all AWS API endpoints' (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/tls-1-2-required-for-aws-endpoints/): as of 2024-02-27 all AWS service API endpoints require minimum TLS 1.2, TLS 1.0/1.1 deprecated
3.1.1.notes: TLS 1.2 is the enforced floor on all AWS service API endpoints; TLS 1.3 is supported and negotiated where the client allows (AWS recommends 1.3, current SDKs default to it). 'TLS 1.2' selected as the guaranteed standard; note the 1.3 support in the cell comment if the form allows. Sources are AWS documentation/announcements surfaced in domain-restricted search; direct fetch blocked. | restored per tim@tavus.io decision 2026-07-31: vendor source URL cited; sandbox network prevented re-fetch, not a content dispute. | Corroborated by AWS SOC 2 Type 2 (Apr 2025 - Mar 2026), p.89: "Customers should use encrypted (TLS/SSL) connections for all of their interactions with AWS. 3.1.2.locator: S3 user guide, server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3): 'uses 256-bit Advanced Encryption Standard Galois/Counter Mode (AES-GCM)' / 'one of the strongest block ciphers available, 256-bit Advanced Encryption Standard (AES-256)'; all new S3 object uploads encrypted by default since 2023-01-05
3.1.2.notes: Documented as AES-256-GCM; encryption at rest is on by default for S3 (where Tavus-stored recordings/media would live). 3.1.3.locator: AWS Backup developer guide, 'Encryption for backups in AWS Backup': 'When AWS Backup independently encrypts a backup, it uses the industry-standard AES-256 encryption algorithm', controlled via the AWS KMS key on the backup vault; cross-account/cross-Region copies automatically encrypted
3.1.3.notes: Scope caveat: this documents the AWS Backup service (customer-configured backups AES-256 via KMS) and backups of encrypted source resources inherit encryption. AWS does not publish a single statement covering every internal backup path, so treat as low confidence and confirm Tavus's actual backup configuration; falling back to 'Not known' would also be defensible. 3.1.4.locator: S3 SSE-S3 documentation: 'Amazon S3 encrypts each object with a unique key. As an additional safeguard, it encrypts the key itself with a key that it rotates regularly' - default keys are generated and managed by AWS

For customer content stored in AWS services used by Tavus (S3, etc.): are ALL backups/replicas made by AWS of that content encrypted, and with which algorithm (we understand AWS Backup uses AES-256 via KMS - does this hold for internal replication/backup paths)?
